chapter.li: Verse20 Now, as I was saying, after king Mosiah had done these things, he took the brass plates and everything he had kept — all the records and the Interpreters as well — and conferred them on Alma’s son Alma, and commanded him to maintain and protect them, adding to the record of the people. He was to hand them down from one generation to another, just as they had been handed down since Lehi left Jerusalem. VerseEnd

LEChapter29 Verse1 When Mosiah had done this, he sent a message across the land, asking the people who they wanted as the next king. VerseEnd Verse2 And the people voted and said: We want 2PSI your son Aaron to govern as our king. VerseEnd Verse3 But he had left for the land of Nephi; so the kingdom couldn’t be conferred on him. Besides, Aaron declined the kingdom anyway, and none of Mosiah’s other sons were willing to take upon themselves the kingdom, either. VerseEnd Verse4 Therefore king Mosiah again sent a written message, asking: VerseEnd Verse5 My people or my brothers and sisters — because I consider 2PP you to be that — I want 2PP you to think carefully about what 2PP you decide. 2PP You want to have a king. VerseEnd Verse6 But I tell 2PP you that the one to whom the kingdom rightly belongs has declined and won’t assume control of the kingdom. VerseEnd Verse7 Now if someone else is appointed in his place, I’m afraid that conflicts would arise among 2PP you. And who knows if my son, to whom the kingdom does belong, might become angry and draw away part of the people to follow him — causing wars and conflicts among 2PP you, which would lead to loss of life and turning away from the Lord’s way, destroying many souls. VerseEnd Verse8 So let’s be wise and think carefully about these things. Because we don’t have any right to destroy my son or anyone else who might be appointed in his place. VerseEnd Verse9 If my son were to go back to being prideful and to his prior foolishness, he would change what he decided and claim his right to the kingdom, which would lead in turn to many sins. VerseEnd Verse10 So let’s be wise, look to the future, and do what will bring peace to this people. VerseEnd Verse11 Now I’ll be 2PP your king for the rest of my days.

Nevertheless, let’s appoint judges to judge this people according to our law, and we’ll reorganize society. We’ll appoint wise men to be judges who will judge the people according to God’s commandments. VerseEnd Verse12 Now it’s better for a man to be judged by God than by man — because God’s judgments are always just, but mankind’s judgments aren’t always appropriate and fair. VerseEnd Verse13 Therefore if it were possible for 2PP you to always have righteous men as 2PP your kings, who would establish God’s laws and judge this people according to His commandments, if 2PP you could always have men for 2PP your kings who would act just like my father Benjamin did for us — I tell 2PP you that if this could always be the case, then it would be fine for kings to rule us. VerseEnd Verse14 I myself have labored with all my strength to teach 2PP you God’s commandments and establish peace throughout the land, so there wouldn’t be any wars, conflicts, theft, plunder, murder, or any kind of iniquity. VerseEnd Verse15 And I’ve punished whoever has committed iniquity according to the crime they’ve committed and according to the law our forefathers gave us. VerseEnd

Verse16 Now I’m telling 2PP you that because not all men are just, it isn’t good for 2PP you to have kings rule over 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse17 Because one wicked king causes so much iniquity to be committed and so much destruction! VerseEnd Verse18 Remember king Noah, his wickedness and abominations, and the resulting wickedness and abominations of his people. What great destruction fell upon them! Because of their iniquities they were also brought into slavery. VerseEnd Verse19 If it hadn’t been for the intervention of their all-wise Creator — because of their sincere repentance — they would have inevitably remained in slavery until now. VerseEnd Verse20 But He rescued them because they humbled themselves before Him; because they prayed humbly to Him, He rescued them from slavery. And this is how the Lord’s power is manifest in all cases among mankind, extending the arm of mercy toward those who put their trust in Him. VerseEnd

Verse21 Now I tell 2PP you: 2PP You can’t remove an iniquitous king from power without terrible conflict, bloodshed, and killing. VerseEnd Verse22 Because he has his friends in iniquity, and he keeps his guards around him, and he violates the laws of those who have ruled in righteousness before him, and he ignores God’s commandments. VerseEnd Verse23 He enacts laws and forces them on his people — laws made according to his own wickedness. And he executes whoever doesn’t obey his laws. He sends armies against anyone who disobeys him; and if he can, he’ll kill them. And so an unrighteous king corrupts and perverts the ways of all righteousness. VerseEnd Verse24 Now I tell 2PP you: Such abominations are avoidable. VerseEnd

Verse25 Therefore choose for yourselves judges by 2PP your vote, so that 2PP you can be judged according to the laws that have been established by our forefathers, which are good and were given to them by the Lord. VerseEnd Verse26 Now it’s not common for the majority of the people to want anything contrary to what’s right, but it’s common for the minority to want what isn’t right. So 2PP you must observe this principle and make it 2PP your law, to do 2PP your business by the majority vote of the people. VerseEnd

Verse27 And if the time comes that the majority of the people choose iniquity, then that is when God’s judgments will fall upon 2PP you and He’ll cause great destruction, just like He’s done upon this land up until now. VerseEnd Verse28 Now if 2PP you have judges and they don’t judge 2PP you according to the law that’s been given, 2PP you can make them be judged by a higher judge. VerseEnd Verse29 And if 2PP your higher judges don’t make righteous judgments, 2PP you must cause a small number of 2PP your lower judges to convene, and they should then judge 2PP your higher judges based upon the vote of the people. VerseEnd Verse30 I’ve commanded 2PP you to do these things to respect the Lord; I’ve commanded 2PP you to do these things and to not have a king, and if these people commit sins and iniquities, they will be responsible for them. VerseEnd Verse31 I tell 2PP you: The sins of many people have resulted from their kings’ iniquities; therefore their iniquities are their king’s responsibility. VerseEnd

Verse32 I don’t want there to be any more inequality in this land, especially among my people. But I want this land to be a land of liberty and for everyone to enjoy their rights and privileges equally, so long as the Lord sees fit to allow us to live and to possess the land as an inheritance, and for as long as any of our descendants are on the land. VerseEnd Verse33 King Mosiah wrote many more things to them, explaining all the trials and troubles of a righteous king: the worrying for his people and the people’s complaints to their king; he explained it all to them. VerseEnd Verse34 He told them these things shouldn’t be like this, but the responsibility should rest on everyone and everyone should do their part. VerseEnd Verse35 He also explained the disadvantages they labored under by having an unrighteous king rule over them: VerseEnd Verse36 the risks of iniquities and abominations, and the wars, conflicts, slaughter, theft, plunder, whoredoms, and all kinds of sin which can’t all be named, telling them these things should be avoided by them, that they were directly contrary to God’s commandments. VerseEnd

Verse37 After king Mosiah sent this message to the people, they were convinced it was true. VerseEnd Verse38 So they gave up their desire to have a king and became very eager for equality for all. And everyone said they were willing to be responsible for their own sins. VerseEnd Verse39 So they assembled in groups throughout the land to vote for judges who would judge them based upon the given law. And they celebrated the liberty bestowed upon them. VerseEnd Verse40 Their love for Mosiah grew — indeed, they regarded him more highly than any other man. They didn’t see him as a tyrant who was seeking power and money that corrupts the soul. He hadn’t demanded and taken their wealth from them or casually killed others, but he had established peace in the land and allowed his people to be freed from all forms of slavery. So they cherished him as a leader. VerseEnd Verse41 And they appointed judges to rule over them, or to judge them according to the law, by voting throughout the land. VerseEnd

Verse42 Alma, the high priest, was appointed to be the chief judge, his father having conferred the office upon him and given him responsibility over all the congregation’s dealings. VerseEnd Verse43 Now Alma walked in the Lord’s ways, kept His commandments, and passed righteous judgments. And there was continual peace throughout the land. VerseEnd Verse44 And so began the judges’ rule over the land of Zarahemla among all the people who were called Nephites; and Alma was the first and chief judge. VerseEnd

Verse45 Now his father died at age 82, having lived to fulfill God’s commandments. VerseEnd Verse46 And Mosiah died too, at age 63, in the 33rd year of his rule. In total, it had been 509 years since Lehi left Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse47 And that ended the rule of kings over the Nephites; and Alma’s days also ended, who was the founder of their congregation. VerseEnd
